name: southern
note: The Southern Pines pack on Meshy, the second of the US golf courses' landscapes (the owner, 6 November 2026): Augusta, Pinehurst, Pine Valley. Sizes and trunk widths are PLACED from each tree's usual form and the owner's course photos. Targets match the Redwood Coast's and Classic Parkland's: 12,600 triangles for a pine, 12,000 for the dogwood. Lessons from Classic Parkland are in the prompts: no even tiers, and nothing fine and hanging, which did not survive the model step. Foliage stays on meshy-6. The first longleaf pictures drew fine needle bursts, which the owner sent back so the model step could keep them: they are now large solid masses. Shipped in vendor/blender-meshy_southern as SouthLoblolly, SouthLongleaf, SouthWhitePine and SouthDogwood, because the hand-built models hold the plain names. `seasons` are PLACED, read by tools/blender/dump-tints.mjs. Eastern white pine was too thin on the first try, so the owner had it redrawn in the longleaf's language.
style: Stylised cartoon game art in soft, flat painted colour. Simple clean shapes with a gentle gradient: darker near the trunk and under each bough, lighter toward the tips. Matte, muted natural palette. No photographic detail, no photo bark, no noise, no speckle, no hard shadows, no highlights, no shine, no ink outlines, no text.
view: One view only, seen from the side at eye level, the whole plant in frame from foot to tip with a margin around it, centred, on a plain white background, in even soft light, with no cast shadow.

models.name: Blender_LoblollyPine_1
models.prompt: A mature loblolly pine tree on a southern golf course, 30 m tall and 10 m wide. A very long straight red-brown trunk with large flat plates of bark, completely bare for its lowest three fifths. Above that a rounded open crown: eight to twelve thick tapering limbs angle upward and fork. Each limb ends in one large solid rounded tuft of foliage, like a soft fluffy cloud, about as tall as it is wide, with a lightly tufted scalloped edge. The tufts are chunky, overlap only a little, and together make a loose oval head sitting high on the trunk, with a bumpy outline and sky between them. Paint the foliage as thick, solid three-dimensional forms, never as separate needles or leaves: no fine needles, no visible leaves, no leaf shapes, no fine detail, no thin lines, no thin wisps, nothing thinner than a limb. No solid core, no perfect spheres, no flat discs, no even tiers of branches, no Christmas tree outline, no cones. A slender trunk, one twenty-fifth of the tree's height wide near the ground, narrowing gently to two-thirds of that width at mid-height and to thick limbs at the top, its sides never parallel. Only a small flare in the very bottom of the trunk, no wide base. Whole healthy tree, no broken or snapped top. Stylised cartoon game asset, matte hand-painted colour. Single tree alone, no ground, no base, no text.
